sites.name: Piasa Bird Memorial
sites.description: In 1673, Marquette and Jolliet observed two monsters painted on the limestone bluffs overlooking the Mississippi River; the current image is reconstructed from more recent lore.
sites.notes: Current painted pictograph is at Piasa Park, less than a mile north of downtown Alton on Illinois Route 100; outdoor site with no visitor center.

sites.name: Lewis and Clark State Historic Site
sites.hours: Interpretive Center: Wed-Sun 9AM-5PM; Store of Discovery: Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun 10AM-2PM; closed Fri
sites.description: Lewis and Clark established a winter camp in December 1803 near Hartford prior to starting their more than two-year journey of western exploration of the Louisiana Territory; gallery exhibits include a 55-foot full-scale replica of their keelboat.

sites.name: South Roxana Mounds
sites.address: Dad’s Club Park, Daniel Boone Trail and Smith Ave
sites.description: Two mounds that may date to the Middle to Late Woodland period are visible within the park.
sites.notes: Memo identifies the mound location as Dad’s Club Park at Daniel Boone Trail and Smith Avenue.

sites.name: Madison County Historical Museum
sites.description: Exhibits in a restored 1836 home include Native American and pioneer artifacts.
sites.notes: Memo notes new exhibits are being designed and developed in the historic house; confirm exhibit availability before visiting.

sites.name: Horseshoe Lake State Park
sites.description: The nearly 3,000-acre park area was inhabited by Native Americans as early as 10,000 years ago and includes the Horseshoe Lake platform mound dating to the Mississippian period (AD 1000-1200).
sites.notes: Memo recommends revising the guide text to note that a Mississippian platform mound is located within the park, though it is now heavily overgrown.

sites.name: Cahokia Courthouse State Historic Site
sites.description: Originally constructed by the French about 1740, the Cahokia Courthouse served as the center of political activity in the Northwest Territory in the late 18th century; WPA excavations in the 1930s are included in the courthouse exhibits.
sites.notes: Municipality naming may need confirmation because Cahokia and nearby municipalities were later merged as Cahokia Heights.

sites.name: Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site & Interpretive Center
sites.hours: Grounds: dawn-dusk; Interpretive Center: hours vary / confirm before visiting
sites.description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site preserves 2,200 acres of the largest pre-contact American Indian community north of Mexico; the original site covered nearly 6 square miles, included 120 mounds, and at its peak around AD 1050-1150 had a population of 10,000 to 20,000 people of the Mississippian culture.
sites.notes: Contact sheet lists the grounds as open dawn to dusk and the Interpretive Center schedule as pending or variable.

sites.name: Emerald Mound
sites.address: Emerald Mound Road via IL Route 4
sites.description: Owned by the State of Illinois, the largest of the three remaining Mississippian mounds in this group is a large flat-topped pyramid about 20 feet high.
sites.notes: From Lebanon, take IL Route 4 north to Emerald Mound Road and turn east; the mound is to the south, with a driving loop available via Emerald Mound Grange Road and Midgley-Neiss Road.

sites.name: Fort de Chartres State Historic Site
sites.hours: Grounds: sunrise-sunset daily; Museum/display buildings: Tue-Sun 9AM-4:30PM, closed holidays, staffing dependent
sites.description: Visitors to the museum in the king’s storehouse at Fort de Chartres can see many eighteenth-century archaeological artifacts relating to the French occupation of Randolph County.

sites.name: Modoc Rock Shelter
sites.address: County Route 7, 2 mi SE of Prairie du Rocher
sites.description: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places and a National Historic Landmark, the sandstone bluff at Modoc Rock Shelter provided shelter for Native American groups beginning shortly after the Ice Age and continuing for almost 8,000 years.
sites.notes: Archaeological landmark site; public interpretation is limited and visit logistics are not clearly published.

sites.name: Fort Kaskaskia State Historic Site
sites.hours: Grounds: 7AM-10PM year-round; Guided tours: Mon-Fri 8AM-3:30PM by contacting the site
sites.description: The 200-acre bluff-top park includes the remnants of a French earthen-work and timber fortification constructed in the mid-1700s.

sites.name: Randolph County Museum
sites.notes: Earlier working file used a different phone number; this version restores the guidebook contact.

sites.name: Piney Creek Ravine State Natural Area
sites.description: Piney Creek Ravine contains the largest body of prehistoric rock art in Illinois, with almost 200 designs believed to date to the Late Woodland (AD 500-1000) and Mississippian (AD 1000-1550) periods.
sites.notes: Current contact sheet uses the Campbell Hill address; the 2014 guide listed a Chester care-of address and county-line directions.
